This is the first [b]thumbs down[/b] I've given in a review, because normally I just wouldn't review a game [i]at all[/i] if it would be thumbs down. This is a rare kind of [i]borderline case[/i]. This isn't going to sound like a nice comment, and in many ways [i]it isn't[/i], but: what made this game [i]worth playing[/i] was that I bought on the Summer Sale [i]for [u]$9.00[/u][/i]. For $9, sure, [b]thumbs up[/b]. For it's normal price point of $60? [b]Thumbs way down[/b].

[h1]What's the Deal?[/h1]
The [i]elevator pitch[/i] version of the game is that, "[i]It's Dead Space, but worse.[/i]" That rings true to a very real degree, but it doesn't [i]really explain the problem[/i]. So here's a problem-focused pitch: "[i]It's a game where they made Beta v1.0, but then they stopped further development; they just fixed the bugs, put on the polish, and released it.[/i]"

The combat [i]especially[/i] feels like that. It feels like they never went, "[i]Alright, here's the first pass done. Now: what works, and what doesn't? How do we elevate it? How do we iron it out and make it better?[/i]" It's literally like they realized late in develop that they hadn't added combat yet and so multiple different teams stuck in combat mechanics and ideas without consulting each other, because there are some mechanics that just [i]straight up conflict with each other[/i].

To explain: the game is melee focused with [i]some[/i] firearms support. Ammo is not [i]entirely[/i] scarce, but it isn't plentiful either, so much of the time you beat on enemies with your melee weapon to save on ammo, and use it sparingly with the game's '[i]quick shot[/i]' feature to blast them once or twice while their reeling for extra damage. Melee combat flows like this: the enemy rushes at you to melee you, and so long as you are holding [i]left[/i] or [i]right[/i], you will dodge automatically in respective direction. If the enemy follows-up with a second swing (or third, or fourth, etc.) you have to switch to the other direction to continue to dodge (i.e. if you dodged [i]left[/i] on the initial strike, you need to dodge [i]right[/i] to avoid the second swing, then [i]left[/i] again for the third, etc.) Once the enemy is through with their attacks, they're briefly open for you to counterattack with your own combo. It's simple and basic, but it [i]does work[/i]. It's definitely a v1.0 kind of system, though. Something to [i]build up from[/i]. And [b]they didn't[/b]. No sir, instead they built and bunch of things [i]that don't work together with it at all[/i]:

[i]* Sometimes an enemy rushes at you and, instead of striking, they will grapple you, leading to a cinematic moment where you have break out by mashing the [b]use key[/b], and you take damage so long as you are in the grapple. [b]The problem is that there is NO TELL WHATSOEVER that they're going to do a grapple instead of a melee strike[/b]. So basically, you're just standing there, waiting for the enemy to rush so that you can dodge and counter, but instead the enemy grapples and gets a little bit of [b]free damage[/b] on you while you mash out.[/i]
[i]* You're encouraged to counter [b]after[/b] the enemy's [b]last[/b] swing of their combo, because that's when they're open. If you counterattack early, you and the enemy will swing at that same time, [b]trading blows[/b], meaning you interrupt each other and both take damage (and health restoration is not super plentiful in the game). However, wait [b]too long[/b] to counterattack after their last swing and the enemy will be ready and [b]block your attack[/b]. The problem is [b]again[/b] that there is [b]no tell[/b] on how many times the enemy will swing, so you're stuck [b]guessing[/b].[/i]
[i]* Later, they add a mechanic where sometimes when an enemy takes damage, a mass of worms will sprout from their chest and writhe there. You're meant to draw your gun and shoot the worms quickly enough, which causes the enemy to take [b]massive damage[/b] and die more quickly than normal. If you [b]ignore[/b] the worms for too long then the enemy will mutate into a stronger, harder form. Essentially, it's a test of making a [b]precision[/b] in the middle of the action, and being punished if you can't. The mechanic is fine and well thought-out... [b]on its own[/b]. The problem is that it [b]doesn't freaking work with the 'quick shot' system[/b] they put in. The 'quick shot' system: when you are striking an enemy with your melee combo, a blue reticle will appear on them; when it does, if you draw your gun it will [b]automatically lock on to reticle[/b], meaning you can fire quickly and ensure a hit. You can [b]guarantee[/b] a pop of extra damage on your enemy for the cost of some ammo, without needing to aim. [b]Well[/b], the worms will sprout when the enemy [b]takes damage[/b], meaning they sprout [b]when you are beating them with your melee attack[/b], which is [b]also[/b] when the 'quick shot' reticle appears. In other words, you see the worms sprout so you draw your gun, [b]but you physically cannot aim at them[/b] because you are [b]locked on to the 'quick shot' reticle[/b], which [b]never[/b] appears over the worms. The two systems [b]work against each other[/b].[/i]

These are just [i]examples[/i] of the problems. They are [i]plenty more[/i], and for the most part they all take this form of an initial idea that was [i]never iterated upon[/i] and [i]never integrated[/i] with the rest of the game. It's a problem of [i]poor mechanical game design[/i].

[h1]So, Is There Anything Good?[/h1]
Yes! The environmental design and atmosphere are [i]fantastic[/i]. On that level, the game simply [i]looks great[/i], too, if you're hardware doesn't have problems with it. And it has [i]cinematic moments[/i] throughout that are well done. The voice actors also do an [i]incredible job[/i], and give stellar performances the whole way through. Likewise, the music is very good, and [i]dynamic[/i], fittings the moments and sequences well.

Other things are middling, which isn't a problem. The story, for example: nothing exceptional, but it does what it was meant to do: carry you along.

[h1]Final Word[/h1]
It feels like a real shame. Like the game got released because "[i]time ran out[/i]" or something like. The game [i]is mostly very polished[/i], so it really feels like they had to suddenly stop development, polish up, and release. If they had just had like [i]two more months[/i], maybe they could have [i]refined their gameplay design[/i] to fix its many conflicting problems, since they otherwise had a good, complete game on their hands.

I'll say it again: "[i]Dead Space but worse[/i]" is the [i]best sell[/i] this game has, so it's only really [i]worth[/i] what a [i]worse Dead Space[/i] would be worth. $9 was [i]fine[/i]. It quickly becomes [i]less fine[/i] for every dollar that cost goes up.

This is the first time I’ve taken the time to write a review. I’ve never disliked a game this much before. 

I wanted to like this game. The graphics are amazing. The sound is even better, but the gameplay made me hate this game by the end. 

I read a review before I bought the game that basically said what I found. For the first few hours, the game seems good. Yes, the combat in the game is very repetitive. Dodge, dodge, strike, strike, repeat until dead (one of you). Then it evolves to add specific targets you must shoot shoot to kill the enemy. Fine. 

By the mid-game it’s getting old and the enemies are stronger, to the point that it is no longer fun. 

By chapter 8 I’m wondering if I care anymore about finishing the game. The point is to have fun and for me, it lost that in chapter 6, if not earlier. Read the reviews carefully before deciding on this game.

TL;DR: Just go play Dead Space.

As much as I respect Glen Schofield, I can't say the same about The Callisto Protocol. According to interview I saw, the game was shipped prematurely, and he couldn’t stop it. The lack of polish is evident throughout, and the story feels incomplete. The final cinematic — and especially the last few minutes — suggests that the full story requires a €15 DLC. A cliffhanger ending that you have to pay extra to resolve is just outrageous.

The combat is dull and repetitive: dodge, melee, dodge, melee — rinse and repeat. It quickly becomes tedious, and the dodging mechanic is frustrating. One wrong move, and you’re dead. I lost count of how many times I was one-shot because the system felt unforgiving.

There’s no map. The level design is linear and sometimes pretends to offer exploration. You’ll find side rooms, but there’s always only one way forward. Worse, it’s not clear which path progresses the story and which is just a dead-end detour. In most cases there will be an autosave indicating that you're now progressing the story, but that will not always be the case. Additionally you will have no space to carry the loot you find in those extra rooms. The environment feel repetitive — everything looks the same. I sometimes got lost, unsure what to do or which object to interact with to progress. And with no objective reminders or prompts, I often forgot what I was supposed to be doing after a break from the game.

Autosaves are terrible. Manual saves are pointless because the game always reverts to the autosave. These saves often happen at the worst moments, killing any sense of pacing. They also scream, "Something big is about to happen!" I’d much prefer save stations like in Dead Space.

The balancing of health and ammo is a mess. Sometimes you’re drowning in resources which cannot carry back because the door is locked behind you, other times you have nothing at all. Just your melee weapon. Maximum ammo capacity is limited, and picking up a new weapon adds another ammo type to juggle. Healing items come in two forms, but the slower one is useless because enemies can interrupt you mid-heal. Why even bother carrying it?

The game’s reflective surfaces are misleading. They often shine like item pickups, leading me to chase phantom loot. Breakable windows and environmental hazards like cysts respawn if you revisit areas, which is ridiculous. Simple things like opening a box can be fatal if your health is low.
The flashlight is another head-scratcher. Its light source seems to come from some tiny, invisible dot on the suit, and it doesn’t even glow. And there is no indication from where the inventory is displayed in front of your character. In Dead Space you at least had a screen built-in front of your suit.

Outfits are lackluster, and inventory space tied to them feels restrictive. The one story-mandated upgrade doesn’t compensate for this. Every chapter transition is interrupted by a black loading screen, shattering immersion.
The intro scene is particularly bad — your character immediately adopts a generic "ready to get jumped" pose, even when there’s no danger. Everyone looks perpetually sweaty, like they’ve run a marathon. Holograms randomly pop up without input, which raises questions: Is there a motion sensor activating these things? Were they turning on every time someone walked by when the station was alive?

The kinesis module (or GRP, as the game calls it) has no clear recharge system. It blinks when it’s low but gives no gradual feedback. You’re stuck waiting around when it’s empty, doing absolutely nothing. Similarly, the inventory system is unnecessarily split into two categories for weapons and then gadgets, ammo and health.

The game is riddled with immersion-breaking bugs. One standout was a giant 2D rat silhouette sliding across the environment. Silent kills are anything but silent, yet enemies remain oblivious even when you kill their buddies right next to them. However, stand up from crouching, and they’ll instantly hear you.

All the weapons look and feel the same. Switching between them is confusing, as you can’t tell what you’re holding. Swapping weapons is painfully slow, and the absence of something as simple as number keys for quick selection is baffling.

The music is almost non-existent. Was this supposed to build tension? If so, it failed. The game isn’t scary. Not once did I feel a moment of fear or suspense, and I’m pretty jumpy.

The difficulty settings are unclear. “Maximum Security” sounded like an option for a safe and secure experience. Nope — it’s just prison terminology.

If you ever wanted Dead Space but with less tension, easier combat, and way more time crawling through vents, here you go.

The game looks and sounds incredible with truly top-tier visuals and audio, and also with varied, spectacular environments. Sadly, the moment you start actually playing, the cracks show fast.

The story? Bland and predictable. Scares? Mostly cheap jump scares. Tension? Almost nonexistent, because combat rewards sprinting straight at enemies and smacking them. Enemies (mostly) politely attack one at a time , dodging is laughably easy, and stealth is a joke: the "blind" monsters are apparently deaf too, letting you stroll up and one-shot them.

The GRP gauntlet is absurdly overpowered - it recharges, it's easy to use, and it can clear most fights without effort. Use it regularly and you'll basically never run out of ammo. New weapons? Just different-shaped guns for the same handful of enemies.

Expect lots of narrow corridors and ventilation shafts where nothing happens, plus a gameplay loop that barely changes from start to finish.

Lastly, performance swings from very smooth to massive stuttering without warning, and there's even a save bug that can wreck your progress (yes, you can fix it externally - I had to).

It's not terrible, but in the end it's a shallow, forgettable game hiding under a gorgeous coat of paint. Fun enough to keep you going, but nothing that will stick. If Steam had a "Mixed" rating, that's where this belongs - but since it doesn't, I lean negative.

The good:

> Graphics.
Yes. That's all

The bad:

> Story. I forgot it even existed. This is a scinematic game yet the story is boring. "go there for the sake of going somewhere". Noone cares. Nothing after nothing happens with explosions everywhere. Only first 30 min were good.
> The first 3 bosses you fight is the SAME EXACT boss. There are 4 boss enounters total. I could not believe. And it's a poorly designed one too.
> The combat system is a gladiator 1v1 lock-system. And for a horror game, it's attrocious from every single aspect. Prime example of how not to design a combat system. You cannot be afraid of what can't lurk behind you. Only jump scares.
> Broken input. Sprinting rarely works. It literally has a mind of it's own.
> Blocking is useless and sets you on a massive dissadvantage. Introduced mechanic and forgotten.

> Enemies wait to attack you when fighting multiple. You can fight one monster for 2 whole minutes while 3 more dance around you. They will never engage.
> A lot of stuttering with shader compiles on a 7950X3D/RTX 4090 system. Even with the added precompile phase, it's really noticable.
> Stealth system is so poor it shouldnt exist. Yet it's forced for hours 'round mid-game.
> No DLSS. Ray Tracing is poorly implemented but it's fine. Couldn't care less with graphics, they are amazing as is.

About hardcore difficulty:
> It is unbalanced with no skill requirement due to the extreme RNG elements. All enemies can do an undodgable instant grabs which make you lose 30+% HP. If you roll bad and they do 4 in a row, you lose automatically. You can't heal mid-fight. And you have to fight 8 enemies in a row per engagement. What are the chances you get grabbed 4 times within 15 minutes of combat? You can get hit 0 times and still lose because you can't dodge grabs .
> Broken economy and bad upgrade system. Getting hit once sets you back 120G in heals where defeating an enemy gives you 5G. On average an upgrade costs ~900 and they give nothing. Why are they even there. Decor?
> You can't run or escape fights. Damn camera lock. If I don't want to fight in hardcore difficulty where health and ammo is this scarse and 80% HP is often 1 hit from death, DON'T FORCE LOCK ME?

When I saw this game get announced, I was excited to all hell. Original lead dev of Dead Space is making what people called a successor, designs that would rival Dead Space, and a story to fuck with your head. Well, at least they were right for one thing in the game, the story is so fuckin bad it really messes with your head. 

If you liked Black Ops 3's campaign and how confusing it was, you'd love this game. It's a confusing story of how the prison was used to experiment on the idea of forced evolution, but did it like in the Doom movie where only certain people would work, and created apex predators that would lead the charge. But that would only create ONE apex predator and what use would that be in the end? You lost billions of dollars, losing all assets to make one break through? And somehow you were the ONLY good one that made it out? Why didn't you change? Because you're good. And the terrorist plot feels oddly forced and rushed. I get the whole thing of attacking a mega-corporation but it's hardly played with and nothing really feels concrete. You see another dude's memories from the beginning and only after you MELD YOUR MIND TO THE TERRORIST SIDE CHARACTER does that start to make sense. It's dumb. 

And the combat is ok? I think they nerfed a lot of the movement and attack canceling since I last played. I can't whack-shoot them as well as I used to. But it was a fun time when I played it. Some moments you feel overwhelmed and doing certain things are immediately stun locked. If you've ever played Silent Hill Homecoming, it's kinda like that. Your attacks get canceled by one hit and you immediately get stun-locked into oblivion until dead, but here it's manageable. Still annoying but manageable. Guns are fun, nothing too big there. They made the guns fun to play around with and having a shortage on ammo is hard to achieve. You'd have to miss A LOT in order for your ammo to be in the red. 

Idk if I want to talk about the DLC since it hurts to even try. If you don't care about spoilers, you died in the end of the game and the DLC is the last moments in the main character's mind. It seemed like it'd promise a sequel or something else after, but it was just to cement the death of Callisto before it even lived. 

Enemy designs are not too great, they're pretty much just a dude that looks fucked up. Not in a fun way either. If you've seen a decrepit hobo on the street, you've seen the design of a majority of the monsters in this game. Some cool ones with really bad names, like one of the fun bosses that is two dudes fused together to make both a nimble and strong monster is called Two-Head. Or the one where it looks like three dudes hugged and fused to make this nimble hunter that can immediately cripple you in a blink that's called a Rusher. Or the one thing that I love that some Sci-fi things do which is give creative model names for robots, I love that so fuckin much. Could call these towering security bots something like Nomads or something that would correlate with the prison like BIPs or Black Iron Drones, but nah. Security Robot sounds fine. 

TL;DR It's a big disappointment that feels rushed out the door and doesn't have much going for it. It's a decent game, but not Silent Hill Downpour decent. Feel bad for the people involved and wish they were given a better chance. 4/10

The Callisto Protocol is such a waste of time, I'm not even sure I want to dedicate mine to review it frankly...but I must inform people; 

The Callisto Protocol is essentialy an amalgamation of poorly designed and badly executed game mechanics that went half-cooked from its conception to the game release; what kinda works in it, it's just because the same hands that made TCP also did [u]the game[/u] that took massive "inspiration" from, which is pretty peculiar seeing that the guy in charge, in retrospective, tried to do THE SAME damn game all over again, giving it another name. From the plot to some mechanics, the similarities are so uncanny, that I can't even classify it as a "spiritual successor".

The melee combat system with the baton has no excuses to be this bad; the worst mechanic in the game by far, which extends every single fight, on hard difficulty, by at least thirty seconds in which you have to dodge and attack without any effort at all in the hope it will all end sooner than later. It gets repetitive after the second encounter if you do not implement anything else with it, but it is almost mandatory to go full melee, because of the scarcity of ammo and resources found in some chapters of the game. At least some weapons feel powerful despite enemies being very lacking in diversity, not offering much of a challenge throught-out the game.

Can't say nothing bad about graphics, we are so far above what we used to look at a few years back, that now, with the high fidelity and the photorealism, good graphics are not a novelty anymore for big companies rather than just something pretty to look at, if the game doesn't just stand on itself, and The Callisto Protocol got too many downsides for that. It runs a bit poorly, as it was already established in the launch days, and even tho it has been fixed somehow in time, it still stutters in some scenarios.

The story starts decently and it is generally interesting on paper but you're almost left out of it as the protagonist for so long, that it starts to feel like it is dragged out, until it fades in an anti-climatic ending if you don't play one of the DLCs that exists only to delve into important details omitted in the base game (and by omitted details I mean that the game goes from one hundred to zero mph in the frame of a minute leaving you with a bitter taste in your mouth, without much explanation). 

Overall a sluggish, forgettable and uninspired experience, if not one of the most useless games I've ever played. It doesn't almost never happen to me, but I had to force myself to finish it while rushing to the end because it was unbereable to keep playing, yet I still wanted to see where the story lead. 

It's so ironic to me that the same year came out the Dead Space Remake too, and it's so much better in every aspect if inevitably compared to The Callisto Protocol, which doesn't manage to check anything positively in spite of Dead Space. 

If you value your time, this is a [b] big skip[/b]. You'll thank me later.

After two playthroughs of the main story, I don’t think The Callisto Protocol is good. "Frustration The Video-Game." The very core of this thing is too flawed. The first half of the game I was convinced this was just not good at all. But…eventually...I admit that despite its many many MANY issues, something about it did come through to me by the end. So while I can’t recommend it at full price, I think on a sale there is something genuine here worth experiencing one day.

Callisto Protocol’s level design is pretty on the surface, but mechanically the more important things are plain, boring, or bad. Graphical fidelity and lighting effects are too good. I’ll say I never get bored looking at this game. Once that trick wares though, there’s not much to grab onto. The entire game is basically one long skinny corridor. If you took any screenshot from the first 5 hours of this game and asked me which chapter it was, I honestly wouldn’t be able to tell you. There’s no backtracking, no unique rooms with memorable sequences, no puzzles, no metroidvania elements, no nothing. Explore if you care about minmaxing. Otherwise you’re not missing anything. It just becomes one linear hallway from beginning to end with a couple branches and hide holes here and there. 

I’m left thinking about what this game’s level design could have been. The devs could have made Black Iron Prison feel more interconnected as a place that had actual structure by making you retread familiar ground and making certain rooms connect to other familiar areas LIKE DEAD SPACE DID BACK IN 2008 FOR CHRIST’S SAKE! Dead Space’s Ishimura was so brilliantly designed. Black Iron prison could have been like that. Instead it has no interest in that sort of mechanical illusion. It feels like a straight line from beginning to end and nothing interesting to see except for pretty graphics and lighting. The exception to this is the game does change it’s scenery with snow and other environments in the later half which made it slightly interesting that I finally wasn’t staring down dark metal hallways anymore. 

Vents...holy crap… I have no idea why the devs thought that making you crawl through 40 plus vents throughout this game was a good idea. Developers, I promise you, vent crawling isn’t fun. It’s a little claustrophobic the first couple times you make me do it in a horror game, but once you’ve made me do it 6 times in the span of an hour and nothing ever happens, then the jig is up. Not to mention, you’re trying to tell me in the far future when we have colonies on other planets, you want me to believe this maximum security prison has huge open vents you crawl through constantly and can reach with your arms everywhere? Seriously?

The story can be summarized the same way I summarized the level design. Cosmetically on the surface it’s good. Its presentation is great with great cutscenes and voice acting. It’s when you look at it closer and expect more depth is when you realize there’s not much there. The characters aren’t that interesting and there’s no plot development until the second half of the game. By the end I did find myself interested enough in the plot, I was intrigued, and I was even invested in the 2 lead characters hoping they would survive. It just took too long to start feeling that way. I’m surprised the game was able to get me to feel that so far in though after a lot of boredom with the story.

Now I could have forgiven a lot of what I’ve talked about so far if the combat was good. But the combat is what done it. Combat is…an absolute abortion. Now, once again just like everything else in this game, its surface level stuff is fun. Animations, finishers, blood and gore, sound effects, that’s all in isolation pretty great. How the combat actually works though and programmed in functionality is a mess. This melee focused combat works fine enough early on when you only fight one enemy at a time but it’s more boring. When the game decides later to throw more than one enemy at you though, it completely breaks, however it's more fun at that point. When you push the attack button to hit an enemy, Jacob locks into an animation with one enemy. So if you’ve got 2 enemies in front of you and you swing between them to try and hit them both, the game will lock you onto one of them, turn you towards them and put you into position so the animation looks better. All other enemies in the arena will simply wait their turn next to you while you’re wailing on one enemy. These are zombies, they wouldn’t wait like that they would just all rush you at once. The devs clearly realized they didn’t create a combat system that can account for more than one enemy at a time very well so they made enemies just stand around while you’re executing melee hits on one enemy until your combo is over. You know what game created a combat system that gave you tools to crowd control and even let you get creative with how you do it AND the space zombies would all rush you at once? Dead. Space. 

Animations won’t even work sometimes. I have so many clips where a zombie starts their attack animation then I decide to attack and see if I can interrupt them. My swing then goes right through them and doesn’t make contact, and then after that instead the game prioritizes the enemy's attack to connect. Why? Because he started his attack before me. So to the game, it doesn’t matter that my attack should have landed first and I should have stunned him, therefore interrupting his attack. Nope. Doesn’t matter. Utterly broken. Also in this game you’re supposed to dodge left, dodge right, dodge left, then hit the enemy a few times, rinse and repeat. The camera during this completely sh**s the bed. The camera jolts everywhere because of the dodge mechanic, and what makes it even worse is that you’re in these narrow corridors most of the time which even further screws with the camera while it’s jolting around during combat. Absolutely atrocious. F minus. Failure. I award you no points developers of this combat. 

I admit though…eventually when I unlocked more moves, some guns, and got the entire combat sandbox revealed to me, I would be lying if I said I never had fun with this broken a** combat. It can be fun in the second half of the game. See the trend here? It’s just a system built too much on making animations connect perfectly for realism’s sake rather than focusing on hit boxes and making the system feel fair.

Look…this game is thin at its core and even broken mechanically. However, even after all of that, I think the reason why I kind of enjoyed it by the end is that this is a game with a lot of effort behind it. I saw it everywhere. The effort and passion is there, and it shows. These guys who made this game are not trying to rip you off or offer you a scam. There’s no insidious plot to get you addicted to spending endless time playing a soulless microtransaction trap. No! It’s just an honest to goodness video game made by people trying to give you an experience worth your money. And so I’m happy some people are coming back and giving this game a little more love than it got at launch. Each of these elements started to glimmer towards the latter half of my playthrough. There’s something to be said about that. The combat at the beginning was boring and repetitive. The level design was disappointing in the first half and waaayyy too many annoying damn vents. The story was basically nonexistent and didn’t move at all for the first half of my playthrough. ALL. Of. Those. Things. Got better, more fun, more entertaining, by the second half. They still had problems, but it started to come together at the end for me. There’s something there. For what it’s worth I started to fall for this game. But I think these devs just made some bad creative decisions early on in this process and it really crippled the core of this thing.

I started Callisto Protocol with a clear head and no real expectations, being both a fan of survival horrors and sci-fi genre in general. I have finished the base game [spoiler](and if I buy a DLC, call 112 because I got a stroke)[/spoiler] but from half of it I felt forced to do so and I can not recommend the game.
I have played a game on hardcore difficulty and from what I have noticed it has a lot of good ideas but everything seems to be... half baked.

1. Melee aspect of the game is interesting at the start unless you understand that almost every single fight is "dodge 2 or 3 times, couple of light attacks, repeat till enemy is dead", the dreaded mutation is actually making the fight only slower because nothing changes except for enemies health. Are you afraid to be ganked by a group of enemies? Well, no need to worry because they always form a queue waiting for a beat-up, just like in old Assassin's Creed and even if the other enemy decides to focus on you, the one you are fighting right now will back out and wait in line.

2. Projectile weapons suck because outside of special "QTE" like moment during the fight they do unsatisfactory amount of damage and you need to save ammo for the "bosses", which 3/4 times is the same enemy with the same attack pattern that will absolutely shred you in melee combat.

3. Do you remember the amazing idea of limb cutting in Dead Space? This one has it too but it does absolutely nothing except changing the attack pattern to one dodge only when the enemy has one limb! Amazing, isn't it?

4. The plot is a standard set of genre cliches which is not bad in itself, but yet again, it's half baked. Most of the story is rushed with nothing explained particularly well, and the Callisto apparently has an atmosphere, snowfall, bearable temperatures (protagonist survives more than 10-15 seconds without a mask which would be death sentence in hard vacuum), EARTH LIKE GRAVITY while in real life it has roughly 12% of it. But hey, it got explained in one 2 sentence video log - you might not even find it if you are not careful - with a magical word "TERRAFORMED". And no, if you expect the rest of the story to make more sense, you are very naive.

5. Level design is for worms, I mean 90% of a level is a linear tunnel and rarely present junctions usually allow you additional 2-5 minutes of exploration.

6. Jacob, the protagonist, has basically no personality whatsoever, which is amazing because Dead Space 1 Isaac Clarke was mute, yet he was more likeable than this guy. Half of the game I couldn't even remember his name and I am pretty certain I will forget it by tomorrow. At least he dies in cool, Mortal Kombat like fashion.

7. Bugs, bugs, bugs. My favourite one is the art of chair- and bedomancy, you can use the gravity gun to push enemies on top of furniture, if the game detects they are in spot they are not supposed to be, they will instantly die. Saved me a lot of ammo! Also, some enemies without eyes can't see you, others have sonar vision. There is no consequence in the enemy design at all.

8. Game economy. Out of 5 guns available in base game, you are handed only 2, the rest of it you can print in crafting station, which is nice but I couldn't afford it even once, split between GRP, melee upgrades and a constant supply of ammo for bosses (maybe I went into wrong "build" but the game never warned me I am making a mistake, it actually encouraged use of melee for the most of playthrough.

5. This one is subjective but I, not even once, felt dread or fright, even a little chill playing it. I still remember the chills of exploring Dead Space Ishimura or Alien Isolation's Space Station, I still remember the clip I emptied because one of supposed victims raised a hand to me pleading for help in the first game, and the alt+F4 combined with a real life scream in one moment of the second game... This one? I felt hopeful for the first half, irritated for the second.

6. Biophages are "we have necromorphs at home". Nothing else to say.

7. The good stuff: graphics (if you care) is mostly consistent and playing it on ultra was eye candy. It contained Licorice and anise, but still.

So, [b]to sum up that wall of text[/b], I am truly disappointed, it was supposed to be a new Dead Space, and all I have is hollow, ill-judged game, where every piece of puzzle of making a nice experience is theoretically here, but if you look closely, every piece of it is cut improperly.

I got this game free from a recent Humble Bundle and decided to try it out despite all the bad things I've heard of it.  Everything bad you've heard about this game is 100% deserved.  As a fan of Dead Space I wanted to give this a fair try so I completed the single player.  The first thing you'll notice is the combat is atrocious.  It is heavily melee focused and consists of doing the same dodge once or twice and then attack 3 times and repeat.  This is how every encounter goes for at least 3/4 of the game.  It gets very old very quick.

Performance for this game was decent on my system.  Likely since so many patches and fixes have been released since then.  The save system in this game is also garbage.  The only real "save" is when you get a checkpoint.  Anytime you do Save Game, it doesn't actually save the game and it even has some small text to tell you that.  Who thought that would be a good experience?  

The starter pistol is very weak and you get almost no ammo for it.  I played this on the Medium difficulty.  It's not until like half way or so through the game you actually start to get any other weapons.  The last weapon the Assault Rifle you don't get until the second to last chapter.  The best weapon I found was the Riot Shotgun, but even with the upgrades you still can't go around blasting everything.  

The story for the game also fell flat.  The pacing for which you're introduced to new characters and trying to build up characters is very quick.  Due to this I didn't care about any of the characters really.  There's no character development or anything you'd see in a good story.  What disappoints me the most is that there's elements in this game that I feel if done right, they could've actually made a great game.  The story in particular I feel they've got a really interesting concept that just wasn't hashed out correctly.  With so many wrong decisions it doomed the game from the start.

Damn, this is a weird review to write.

During the first 3 hours playing the game, I really wondered why the reviews are only on mixed. I thought that this was such a great game; how could you dislike it. After a few more hours, I now can understand it. So I try to explain what actually happened. 

This game is like one of the most beautiful hikes you ever did. The problem being that your feet are fully covered in blisters. While the story, graphics and especially the level design are all fantastic, the actual gameplay is one of the worst one I have ever experienced. I played the game on maximum security difficulty, mainly with the melee weapon. If you play on a different difficulty or a different game mode in general, this could differ a lot from my playthrough. 

From the 10-12 hours estimated playtime, a good half just consists of fighting enemies. And the fights are what totally kills the game for me. In the beginning, it is quite okay to just press "A" and "D" to dodge enemy attacks to strike back at them. But this is pretty much all that is happening when encountering enemies. Its nearly the same thing every second room. Enemies run to you -> Fight -> "A" -> "D" -> "A" -> 3xLeft Click -> Repeat the dodge. There are some opportunities to kill the enemies a lot faster with environmental hazards or by stealthing, which isnt really fantastic but at least it is something different. No fight in this game is difficult, it just takes its time. That issue is even getting worse when enemies got a special feature about 1/4 into the game that "require" to shoot a special part of them. This could have been interesting if it wasnt for the "feature" that autolocked on enemy limbs and makes it really weird for you to aim at the special parts (You cannot turn this off). The gameplay is just so repetitive and boring that it manages to kill the vibe of the game. 

The atmosphere would be there because the graphics are top-notch, the sounds are neat, and the design overall is nothing but fantastic. But because of the actual gameplay, you will never feel a sense of dread or horror. My best comparison would be "Deadly premonition" where the game just got a combat mechanic the last second before release.

Okay aside from the rambling about gameplay, I really love some things about the game. The graphic- and level-designers really understood what they were doing. Also, even though the story was not the craziest idea ever, I enjoyed it. Especially because of the great actors playing the main characters. These were the reasons I didnt quit the game early on, and also the reason why the game is so infuriating. If it were not for the gameplay, I would have loved this game.

BUT if you manage to play the DLC "Final Transmission", everything from my review changes! Just kidding, the fighting even has a stronger focus here. Still the DLC concludes the base game with an expanded ending, which I liked a lot.

So my conclusion is: You might enjoy this game if you play it on a different difficulty or gamemode (I havent checked those out) and you can ignore the lack of proper gameplay. From the perspective of my own playthrough, I unfortunately cannot recommend it, though.

Literally the only reason I got this game is because I wanted to see for myself if it was as bad as people said, and it was on a huge sale for somewhere around 85% off. It was pretty much as bad as I expected.

The graphics are literally the only good thing that can be said about the game, and even then the PC port is pretty bad. You have access to higher graphics settings but at the cost of the game being buggier. 

I had some objects or environments loading in very delayed, enemies teleporting up or down certain levels of elevation, getting stuck in the air at certain spots, and at one point my saves seemed to disappear which would have cost me hours of progress. Fortunately (or unfortunately depending on how you look at it) it's a common bug and I was able to fix it by starting a new game which caused my saves to become visible again.

Even without the bugs though, the game has lots of problems that make it a mediocre slog to get through. The combat is extremely samey across the whole game, with all enemies but the bosses and the one ranged type being fought the exact same way. It's a tedious affair where you just alternate between holding the stick left or right to dodge then counter-attack when the enemy is done, and the enemies are sponges who take a while to kill, especially on higher difficulties. There are also a few stealth sections, but it's probably the worst stealth I've ever seen competing with Ubisoft in how bad the enemies are at detecting you. The blind ones in particular will basically never notice you as long as you're crouching, touching them or firing a gun are the only way you'll be detected so long as you crouch. It's also very clunky clearly not being designed with multiple enemies in mind, and you have no real control of how the main character moves which can lead to you unintentionally falling off elevated platforms or into death traps that insta-kill you. The GRP (basically kinesis from Dead Space) is also lazily implemented, all you really do with it is throw enemies into generic spike walls placed all over and occasionally toss an explosive canister at them. 

The game is also extremely padded out with tons of crawling and squeezing through tight gaps across pretty much the entire game. There are also various sections where you're unable to run. A large reason for it being done is to give time for characters to talk for the sake of the story, but the story isn't even worth playing through the game for. It's extremely generic, the characters are bland, it's predictable, and it ends on a cliffhanger which was likely intended as sequel bait but just got turned into an overpriced DLC which is apparently just as bad as the main game.

And on top of all that the game simply isn't scary. It seems to try to be with cheap jumpscares earlier on and attempts at some cryptic psychological horror later, but at no point was I ever scared. The gameplay does not lend itself to being scary and it seems like during the middle part of the game they give up on trying to make it scary.

Don't buy this game, just don't. Even for only about $13 CAD I still feel like I wasted my time and money. Cry of Fear, Darkwood, Spooky's House of Jumpscares, Lost in Vivo, all better horror games for much less.

This game is the product of what happens when just having the Creator of a similar series (Dead Space), isn’t enough to create something halfway decent, even though you give him a full, experienced dev team and a huge pool of resources.

Made a mistake having my hopes up back before this came out. Then they were crushed after the 1st wave of reviews. Didn’t touch it for about year. Finally, I recently purchased the Digital Deluxe version @ 18 EUR.

Even though I went into it with the lowest possible expectations, somewhere down, at the bottom of the Marriana’s Trench, they were still dashed. The first 3rd of the game, you are basically thrown right into the thick of it, and you’re like sure, let’s start in an even more explosive fashion than Dead Space. Then you keep waiting for some story to cling on to, but since there isn’t much of it, you only receive very small drips throughout, until way too close to the end, when you get a more complete exposition dump. By that time, you will have either abandoned the game, or when the “revelations” (that you can see coming from miles away) finally arrive, you will be completely unfazed by them, and will simply want to see the credits roll sooner.

The gameplay is not as horrible as everyone makes it out to be, but it’s not Sekiro or even Jedi Fallen Order/Survivor. It's more melee focused than DS, and that’s fine for the most part. The weapons, however, are bland and the standard shooter fare. It’s like they copy/pasted so much of DS (health system, character movement animations, Reforge, stomp system for loot) but they skipped the parts that made that series fun (creative weapon & monster design, dismemberment, etc.). There is barely any dismemberment, you have to shoot or hit the enemies an inordinate number of times, before it finally happens.

Another big mention in the abysmal department is the level design, which is basically just you crawling through vents and navigating the same bland corridors ad nauseum. Like I get the fact that it’s all set in a prison (which conveniently has factories, psych wards, terraforming plants, secret colonies, and others beneath), but damn, is it all uninteresting, barely visible. There are only a few sparks of creative level design throughout. It’s all a big shame, because Unreal Engine 4 is actually used very well on a technical level (mostly because the levels are small and corridor-like).

The DLC doesn’t make everything worth it, and even though there are a few decent, creative narrative ideas in there, which in-of-themselves are not bad, still can’t do much to aid the fact that you’re basically kept in the dark to hide the fact that there is very little story to digest, and you’re just being drip-fed small portions of it, with a promise of a future franchise (which will likely never come now). It’s a really shame, because the gameplay improves a bit through more variety, you get a new weapon, enemy type and some new (DS like kinesis) abilities.

Would not replay, and would not recommend, even if you’re starving for a decent survival action horror. This just isn’t it.

What started out as a mildly interesting space-horror game, quickly turned into endless corridor walking, shimmying and dodging.

The game nails the atmosphere ... or can nail it if it decides to actually show you some varied environments. Graphics are jaw-dropping, the violence is super gory, presentation is fine, really.

The story is ... well, it exists, but Jesus himself would've fallen asleep. It's just so ... I just couldn't care anymore after a while. 

All of that is largely unoffensive. We didn't encounter any real bugs or anything, but the major issue in this game is, unfortunately, the gameplay, because it's boring as fuck.
All you basically do is press left/right, then attack. You always automatically dodge. The only difficulty is sometimes figuring out whether you can attack NOW or need to dodge another attack, because that's inconsistent. Multiple enemies on screen aren't really a big difference. Rarely will they actually attack you in tandem. It's more like lemmings to the slaughter.
The game's focus is definitely on melee, so color me surprised when, after putting all my upgrades into melee combat, I encounter an enemy that cannot be killed by any other means than guns ... and that can basically soft-lock your game, because you may simply not have enough ammo, especially if your weapon damage isn't upgraded and you miss a few shots, since you only have time to aim for like 0.5 seconds before he swings at you again. That is a boss enemy. Color me even more surprised when that same boss enemy then appears as a REGULAR enemy THREE more times! Great game design.
The ranged weapons all feel relatively lackluster. Sometimes you can pump an enemy full of "lead" and they just shrug it off, other times they lose heads, limbs, etc. (and still come after you!). Even the upgraded versions lack any kind of impact. That's because the game WANTS you to engage in its bad melee combat system. Satisfying to watch ... for a few times, at least, but clunky.
The "kinesis" module is apparently quite good, but I found it unwieldy to use. Maybe it's fine with MKB, but with a controller I could barely get it to work. It also doesn't help that you can barely see IF you have power left or HOW MUCH!

Couple that with levels that are WAY too long (we're talking like 1.5 to 2 hours for a single level) and consist mostly of slowly walking from point A to B, killing a multitude of enemies and finding a doohicky to open a door, and a save system that shouldn't deserve the name (you basically cannot manually save, despite the game telling you you can ... a manual save resets you to the last auto checkpoint you've passed! Same when you die, which can mean repeating 20 minutes or more of gameplay), and you got yourself a real slog. I'm happy when we're done next session.

And I'm disappointed. Massively. Just play Dead Space instead. The original or the Remaster.

The game focuses so heavily on graphical fidelity that it seems blind to every other aspect of good design. The result feels like overcompensation for inconsistent and tension-free stealth, shallow combat, level design that discourages exploration, bland enemy types, upgrades that do not encourage experimentation, and jump scares that never land. Enemies hit Jacob cheaply every time, no matter how prepared the player is. The Callisto Protocol is not scary. It is not fun. It is not engaging, interesting, or even mildly worthwhile. It claims the style and mechanics of Dead Space but uses none of them with any real skill, creating something that feels like a crude imitation. It plays poorly, it lacks originality, and it treats the player with open hostility. The one jump scare trick it does have is repeated so often that it becomes absurd. It has no business calling itself a worthy successor when it cannot even stand beside the weakest imitators. Playing The Callisto Protocol made me feel like I was wasting my time, and that is not a feeling I often get from games. With repetitive combat and a world that has no tension but plenty of pointless violence, it can go suck an egg.

There are several other instances of interactions feeling Hollow, like something was Meant to be there, but was just... silently removed by the Developers. The incredible amount of Padding serving as its main way to increase how long the players will have to endure before they finish the game.

Most notably of all... This game is extremely easy, it holds your hand throughout every second. Even Combat!
Which makes every victory just feel even More Hollow than the rest of this game.
The best thing about The Callisto Protocol... are its graphics, who are now surprisingly well optimized, in comparison to its initial launch.

Meh... this game tries so hard to be Dead Space, it's actually pathetic... and yeah I'm aware the guy who made Dead Space made this game. EA basically stole his brain child and legal stuff happened and he lost the rights to it... yadda yadda... this is why you hire lawyers before dealing with greedy ass corporations.

All that drama and information aside... this game is just crap. It's like Dead Space except the focus is way more on melee weapons and timing attacks than it is about dismemberment and fun. The combat is also very low brow and juvenile, prison style combat where you're beating a monster to death like he was a human inmate in a prison... I mean that's the theme but honestly... they're monsters we're dealing with here... give me a break.

In Dead Space, there were a variety of weapons, if you were bored of one style, there were like 9 other weapons to choose from. Save points were in abundance and spaced out properly as well as shops / upgrade stations. This game? Absolutely ridiculous... 

You can save where ever you want to but the game forces check points upon you. You could go around collecting stuff, save your game, close it down, restart it 3 days later and be completely lost when you return. So even if you manually save (which I recommend doing) it needs to be near an auto save spot, otherwise you just lose progress and have to get your bearings again upon reload.

It's insanely linear and there are SO many points of no return it's insane. Most areas are a 50/50 path branch and if you take the wrong one (a.k.a. the right one) then you just missed out on something, so reload one of your 9 auto saves and re-do all the stuff you just did... it's a joke and takes you out of the immersion every chance it can... I hate games with missible nonsense... it's so 2007... like get over this crap already and just make a good game...

There's a ton of useless data log's to collect and yes, you can miss all of them. If you do happen to miss something (and you will without a walk through, trust me), you have to start the entire run over again if you've saved past a point of no return.

For some odd reason the developers decided to patch the game and moved around most of these data logs as well... So unless you have an up to date guide, you'll literally be scratching your head as to why the log isn't where the guide says it is. This actually happened to me and prompted me to want to make a negative review right there on the spot. I had to start the entire game over from Chapter 1 and I was in Chapter 3. 

I decided to not be so harsh and played for a few hours longer and then it really hit me how bad this game is. I was finding all kinds of loot and there were no shops a.k.a. "print stations" to locate and sell all of this junk to. You're forced to leave valuable stuff behind in favor of health items and resources like ammo, which means forget ever getting stronger unless you're half dead and used all your health items... it's piss poor design and just way too extreme.

I found 7 or 8 of these energy converter items to sell and there were ZERO shops to sell them to for days. The pacing is absolute garbage and your inventory for resource items is limited to 6 slots for half the game but there are like 9 giant slots for giant weapons, go figure. 

This game is literal hot garbage and these developers are incompetent. I heard bad things about this game's performance when it released so I didn't bother with it, my 5090 Astral OC brute forces this trash, everything maxed out at 185 FPS... so whatever... this game's not even worth a toss, it's so poorly optimized, there's no reason you should need a $4000 video card to run this trash on max settings in 4K... it's inexcusable.

The biggest offense this game committed was right when I bought it. I was missing two of the skins from the deluxe package and I had to MANUALLY create a KRAFTON (wtf even is this company?) account and link my Steam to it... so yeah great start. More security breech points to my Steam account and corporate data acquisitions, so they can steal my information and sell it... lovely... I digress. I had to make this account, link it to my Steam profile and then contact their customer support to unlock these skins that I had paid for...

This was already a red flag but I paid $15 CAD for this p.o.s. so I figured, whatever... it's $15... I mean, a fast food combo costs as much nowadays so I figured I may as well give this a go... yeah, it's awful...  should have just bought a Big Mac and ignored this garbage. 

The game play is bad, the direction is bad, the performance is probably bad as well but I'm rocking the best video card in the world on this thing so I can't exactly gauge this aspect much... either way, total dog sh|t... I'll play it through to the end to see the cliche plot unfold or whatever but my God... this is bad.

I also researched unlockable content and there isn't anything. There are no secret weapons or skins tied to finishing the game on the hardest settings... only achievements... so yeah, this game is a one and done for me... especially considering how linear and boring it is.

The true ending is locked behind the DLC as well, which is just laughable. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME FOR FULL PRICE. Wait for a sale and grab the Deluxe package for the cheapest price possible because man, this game is BAAAAD.

Also, there are cut scenes you can't skip, long winded vent crawling sections, tight narrow walls you have to wedge yourself through and door opening animations that rival the original Resident Evil for loading screen time sinks... you'll be dealing with this crap on EVERY play through... what a waste of life.

They also expect you to beat this game multiple times (just like Dead Space) and they even have a mode, just like Dead Space's Impossible mode, called Contagion mode. If you die on this mode, you have to start the entire chapter over again... which, okay, fair... it's better than the entire game (Dead Space's Impossible mode) but still, it's ridiculous. There are a lot of one shot death areas at the end of most of the chapters as well as bosses that just 1 shot murk you.

I also hate the combat, it's not smooth like it is in Dead Space, it's insanely scripted like one of those Batman Arkham games; except there are no button prompts on screen to take you out of the immersion... but also, it's insanely obvious because of the pauses between attacks. You can't just 5 hit combo an enemy, it's 3 hits, then you have to dodge or block and repeat... it's nauseating how lame this game is.

Your gravity bracer (because yes, they had to copy this from Dead Space as well), that allows you to throw enemies around and grab item boxes, is also terrible in this game. This thing runs out of juice so fast you literally have to make snap decisions and pre-plan where you're tossing these bags of meat... it's almost not even worth doing. Rather than the energy being expended per use, it's literally based on time while in use... so the bar runs out while you're holding enemies... what a garbage design.

Your gun is OP as hell once it's fully upgraded but good luck finding bullets or credits to upgrade this thing. This game is literally 80% melee and 20% ranged shooting. When you reach the final boss, your melee attacks can't damage him and you have to rely on a gun... so you can literally brick your save file if you spent too much on the baton... which you use for 80% of the game... LOLOL... this game is TRASH.

Also, the whole 3D-printing weapons and upgrades is such a 2020 phase, it really dates this game. I remember when everyone and their grandmother were 3D printing crap during covid.

Meh... 5/10 at best... combat sucks, game play sucks, design sucks, pacing sucks, balance sucks. It's not as good as Dead Space. Just go buy the remake of that, you'll have a much better time. If you must play this trash, $15 tops for all the content, other wise you got ripped off.

How about corporation good, band of rebels bad for a change or finding out you've been on the wrong side.

I have played through the campaign, played through the DLC and have played a few rounds of Riot Mode and I think that ive experienced enough now to say this game is terrible and frustrating which is honestly heartbreaking. It oozes potential and an interesting setting as well as an original take on horror combat, that being vicious melee fights.

I feel that posting this review is irrelevant as frankly the whole damn world knows Callisto is not good and missed the mark but dammit these 12 hours have been so miserable that I feel like i needed to throw my likely very unnecessary opinion into the ring. If you want a deeper dive into why this game is as it is, check Youtube, dozens of others now have made longer form essays thats effectively summarize the issues with this game. 

The only thing i want YOU to know is that I have never had a game make me flip flop so rapidly from saying "are you fucking kidding me?" as the game hits you with its 17th cookie cutter slug-thing-in-the-treasure-chest jump scare which didnt even work the first time to playing extreme staring contests with literally crowds of monsters as they send in one dude at a time to play the somehow most boring goddamn game of patty-cake with Jacob.

Between these delightful moments youll enjoy maneuvering Jacob who controls as if bricks are constantly strapped to his body. This clearly comes from a focus on animation fidelity and realism, forcing damn near everything into a crawl and crawls through vents into the movement equivalent of molasses going uphill in winter. On crutches. This slow movement is particularly great when you also discover Jacob runs at the same speed as the exploding crawling enemies essentially meaning if you have no bullets cause, oh idk maybe youre actively using them on the FINAL BOSS you cant create any distance to safely deal with them as theyre consistently up your ass. It took me one attempt to kill the final boss but oh boy it was just a joy and not a constant aggravation. 

These limited animations in combat love to also make you miss as you swing short as the only damn melee weapon your given in this assumed(?) melee focused game is a short baton (not counting the DLC hammer which was actually cool but you get it for 8 seconds at the point where youre likely experiencing aggravation critical mass at the end of this game). And dont you dare try to hit a target before they swing at you first! No no sir, its John Monster-man's turn to swing then you get to go, dont you know this is the space melee equivalent to the American Revolutionary goddamn war? 

I now realize as i type this i am in a anger spiral as more and more things popped into my head that i hated and its really not worth typing, but i dont wanna do that, this is too long already. The only thing you should take from this is that this game is aggressively OK almost all the time with intermittent moments where your frustration will spike with even rarer moments where there is a quick flash of brilliance. To me this anger is tinged with sadness as this game seems to have everything it needs to be amazing to me; setting, combat, themes, everything. And yet it just felt incomplete.  

TLDR: The game is very pretty and its mediocre story is carried by its talented cast of actors. It has interesting ideas but just falls short in execution. Absolutely everything feels like it was made by people that dont know that a video game is also supposed to be a game and not just a tech demo.

DID SOMEONE SAY DEAD SPACE?!?!?


Seriously it's very hard to talk about this game and not mention dead space, considering how much this gane is hellbent on making you remember dead space, which for sure is a much much better game.

I was actually quite excited for this game when it was first announced but when the reviews dropped it instantly killed my hype, doubley so when dead space the remake came out to universal acclaim, and whilst I'm glad I've now finally played it I can safely say the reviews are right, this game isn't really that good despite some really nice graphics.

So before I start moaning too much I do want to say this is probably one of the best looking games I've played and it ran beautifully on my machine, the voice acting as well is really incredible and the overall presentation can't be denied, it's a shame the games world isn't really expanded on because it is presented in a fantastic way. I also can't really complain that this game is bad, it plays well, it runs well and looks incredible. It's one of those awkward games that is stuck on the edge of a thumbs up or down but ultimately I'm giving it a thumbs down.

I really didn't like a few things that being the combat, enemy design, story and atmosphere unfortunately that's the bulk of the game. 

The enemies are so uninspiring and bland that it really kills all tension the game has, the vast majority of time it'll be zombies...just zombies, when you have a cool sci-fi setting you can go crazy with awesome aliens or lovecraftian horror but no we get zombies, oh and a few enemies originally cut from dead space. 

Combat is so bad, it has some fun 3rd person shooting and completely rips off the Kinesis from dead space, the guns are very generic but they at least feel good to shoot, however the main bulk of this game is melee combat which in my honest opinion is just shit, it's spammy with no sense of skill and you are able to cheese it so easy by dodging. It's a system that was patched after launch because it just wasn't right and what we have now just feels so dumb because you just fight one enemy at a time, it really brings this game down and with ammo being so expensive it's a system you will constantly have to engage with. 

I won't spoil the story but have you seen aliens or are you aware of weyland yutani? Well then it's exactly what you expect, yano dead space was cool because it had the marker and cults and body horror and it was all in service to the genuinely interesting plot whilst this game, stuff just happens and it's all hand waved away at the end in one of the most tepid reveals I've experienced in a while. Is this the result of this game originally having ties to PUBG which they backtracked on late on development? Yeah probably but it sucks and the whole setting is wasted. 

I think for me the biggest deal breaker is that this game isn't scary and relies too heavily on cheap jumpscares which don't work and nostalgia from dead space, look at the end of the day if this game is going to spend 90% of the time reminding me of a better game and then 10% of the time annoying me then I'll just go play the better series. Not the worst game I've played and some will enjoy this a fair bit but for me a waste of potential.

I wouldn't have bought it if it wasn't discounted. It's not really worth it, even though it is really good graphics. It has very little to offer apart from really good graphics. And that doesn't really make a game. It's basically a new version of dead space. The story isn't anything special, and once you've completed 20% of the game, the rest of it is exactly the same.

As a solid fan of survival horrors, I'd say this game was onto something, but ultimately did not deliver. I was hoping to get all the achievements for this game but I can't play this anymore.

I do hope for the devs to make a big comeback after this.

It could have been absolutely incredible. But these downright-idiotic design choices hold it back tremendously.

Despite having a positive overall experience, I still wouldn't casually recommend this game to a friend. There are many other games out there that are much better. [h1]The gist of it:[/h1]
Dead Space's true successor is what I'd call Callisto Protocol if it wasn't a crawling simulator that loves to waste your time more than scare you or entertain you. 

👍 [u]The good parts:[/u]
+Decent atmosphere-wise, with some cool locations here and there
+Nice animations and character models

👎[u]The bad parts:[/u]
-One of the worst-paced games I've ever played, so much so that it ruins the entire game
-Garbage story

[h1]Story[/h1]
Remember Dead Space? Its story? I do, even though it wasn't the main focus of the game, it stuck with you forever because of how depressing it was. I forgot the entire Callisto Protocol story after 2 days. It is the most factory-line-made horror story you can think of. 

Without spoiling much, as if you couldn't figure out after 5 minutes what the whole shtick is, you are a smuggler of sorts, things happen, you crash-land on a prison planet where "experiments" happened, and now almost everyone is dead, you uncover what the "oh so shocking" truth about your character did or not do, cliffhanger cheap scare moment, the end. 

The story has more holes than a Tom and Jerry cartoon cheese. There are so many things not explained and while that i usually a good thing for most horror games, Callisto Protocol's holes are just nonsense. You are forced to like an unlikeable douche of a character for the entire game because of reasons. Even the protagonist himself feels out of place at times with what is going around. Environmental story-telling? None of it is to be found. 

Story rating: 5/10

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Let's just get to the bad. Half the game you will be slowly opening doors and walking and crawling in vents or small spaces, and no, this is not an actual exaggeration. I did not believe Steam reviewers and others when they called it out and laughed about it, I too thought they were probably just making fun of a bunch of often fake loading screens, but boy was I SO wrong. 

Once the game goes into combat scenarios, it's pretty decent, nothing remarkable about it especially if you played Dead Space games. It heavily takes inspiration from it since it's from the same original creator, but instead of making it entirely fresh, I suppose he relied on nostalgia. I suppose the melee aspect of it is new, but it's at the same time a mini-game of dodging and hitting the enemies, so much so that it never really feels natural?

It has all the ingredients of all good third-person horror games, but it just doesn't mix them properly. The guns are ok, you can upgrade them and whatnot, but they lack the unique factor, you have like two types of pistols and two types of shotguns, and it all feels very cheaply made. To make matters worse, even their own gravity thingamajig that you use to pull enemies and push them into spikes and whatnot is extremely half-baked.  

Gameplay rating: 6.5/10

[h1]Audio[/h1]
I suppose the only good thing about the game is its overall audio design. Voice acting was probably where all their money went since they hired Hollywood actors and every character plays well. Too bad the scripts were poorly written. 

The soundtrack is pretty much decent, it has the same repeated rifts and drums over and over in combat which almost all action horror games use, but nothing really outstanding, and outside of combat, it does create a bit of tension. 

Sound effects from guns to environments are all pretty good as well and manage to create a decent atmosphere for the players. 

Audio rating: 7.5/10

[h1]Graphics, performance and tech analysis[/h1]
This game has been lauded as a graphical powerhouse and I'll have to disagree completely. Most of the game has fake seamless loading screens, the crawling opening doors, and vent exploring are all loading screens, and it shows as more than half the game that's all you'll be doing. Outside of character models, the level design and textures are quite average. You'll notice a lot of heavy pop-in textures, weird lighting effects, and plenty more gfx that just don't look good. 

Taking into consideration that the level design is extremely linear and you have so many fake loading screens, it's insane how the game can barely run at a decent framerate. Take TLOU2 for example, that game is still one of the best-looking games on the market and it ran on a PS4. There is nothing technically impressive about Callisto Protocol unless this is your first game ever. 

At least the animations and main character models look good especially yours.

Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 6/10

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
The game is always heavily discounted nowadays and even then I'd say stay away from it if you value your time. I honestly can't trust anyone calling this game good or above. You're better off replaying Dead Space or Resident Evil 2-4 Remakes a million times than playing this once. 

[h1]Final score: 6.2/10[/h1]

After 18 hours of playing this game and it's DLC, trying to experience as much of it as possible, here is what I think; I laughed. I cried. but only ever about how terrible this game is...

In all seriousness, I've been trying to think of the best analogy for this game, but I think I've got it:

Remember when you were growing up and you wanted a transformers for Christmas, but your grandma bought you a transmorpher instead?  It broke within a day and the lead paint was likely making you sick?  That's this game...

The game you want is the Dead Space remake, but instead you may have gotten this thinking that with the lead developer/creator of Dead Space, that The Callisto Protocol would be able to encapsulate what made Dead Space such an amazing game.  Well I was frankly shocked at the gross incompetence of this game. 

It attempts to mimic or just outright copy much of the original Dead Space, and does so poorly that I'm amazed to say this, but I think the real talent behind that game was at EA (genuine shocker).  I will attempt to highlight some of the glaring issues this game has:

- The checkpoint system is simply atrocious and geniunely game breaking at times. Imagine losing items picked up BEFORE the checkpoint after respawning.  And it isn't just items, I literally had the game forget to give me audio logs that I picked up before the checkpoint.  Not the least of the checkpoint issues is how infrequent and seemingly random they are, imagine buying a bunch of items in the store, a process which can be fairly tedious and time consuming, then dying, and needing to do it all again, because the devs didn't think to have a convenient checkpoint system that saved at mundane acts like that.

- But here's the kicker, they put in a manual save function in the pause menu.  But guess what, (at least at the time of this review) that manual save system literally just brings you back to the last checkpoint!  It SAYS manual save in the files, but it literally does nothing but load the last checkpoint, making the whole thing pointless.

- The world/maps are just so... videogamey?  Basically, the world is one giant OSHA violation.  LITERAL spike walls dotted around the place that serve seemingly no "real world" function in-context.  Industrial fans that can dice people to bits, that are unprotected and right beside walkways.  Random and unexplained pillars that act as meat blenders to any odd person walking by, and gear systems that are seemingly designed to eat people.  I know these things exist to give players the ability to use environmental kills, but with the subtlety of a nuclear bomb and completely immersion breaking.  It's like the devs didn't even attempt to make the game world "feel" like a real place.

- The "jumpscares" are so predictable and hacky that they're simply astounding as to how bad they are.  Again, much of the concepts behind Dead Space are done here, but to a much worse effect.  Audio triggers are so broken that you can be in an empty room with the music swelling to some peak tense moment, only for nothing to happen, like the game forgot to have enemies or some jumpscare.  Some might say that was intentional to increase tension, but after how many times it happened to no effect, I'm thinking it's just a bug or more incompetence.

- The melee "system" is so easily broken and immersion breaking.  Watching as these foaming-at-the-mouth vicious enemies patiently wait to attack you is so goofy as to be laughable; then when things get tough, the combat camera bugs out and keeps switching shoulders at times as it struggles to figure out which of the 3 enemies standing in front of you is going to attack.  What you are left with is frequent clipping issues as some enemies swing at you while others bug out and sometimes move through each other to not block the death animations.  Additionally, enemies often force grabbing animations, which was also in Dead Space, but in that game you weren't forced (or even encouraged) to go to fisticuffs with every. single. enemy....

-  Relating to the melee system is the dodge mechanic, which once you get the hang of it, trivializes all combat into a repeating cycle of dodge dodge swing swing swing.  And once you have that down, basically all encounters, EVEN BOSS BATTLES are hilariously easy, you can even accidentally dodge bosses by just moving away from them naturally.  I've heard some say that it can get more complex with power attacks and quick gunshots, but those don't really do much, especially in the late game, and what's more, is that it's just so boring after the first 10 mins of the game.

- I seem to remember them boasting, once upon a time during development, about the death animations.  Turns out, pretty much all death animations stem from the same outcome, Jacob losing the front half of his head.  It was again fairly comical watching numerous different death animations, but having the result be exactly the same.  If you want to see how this concept of death animations SHOULD work, go to Dead Space, where there is a dozen or more unique death animations based on circumstance and what enemy you are fighting.

- The voice acting is alright, but the dialogue is boring an uninspired, with the main plot being fairly ridiculous and convoluted.  Now I know some people will say "it's a game bro, it isn't going to make sense", but I disagree.  You can make games with plots that are pretty out there, but its about character motivations and actions that can still keep you immersed in the world.  When characters start doing or saying stupid things, it really breaks the immersion.  In both minor and major ways the story and dialogue are weak, from one character saying "Doesn't matter" when being asked about the monsters running about, to the preposterous inclusion of a secret society/cult, just so they could match plot points from Dead Space, this game's plot and characters are just... weak.

- My mom once said, "If you don't have anything nice to say, then don't say anything at all"... Well my mom never played this game.  I struggle to think of A SINGLE THING that this game does well.  I've heard some say the graphics are a plus, but not really.  Sure, the game looks fine, but it doesn't do anything to make it stand out, at least not compared to any other games and especially not for the time.  But considering the performance bugs that STILL plague the game at times, and I'm left with about nothing positive to think of that I liked about the experience.


Now I've brought up Dead Space several times and that's because it is abundantly clear that this game was trying to "cash in" on that games good name.  Its in the setting, with confined spaces and odd noises (attempting) to create tension; its in the enemy types and the rough approximation of the gore of their very being; its in the plot with unsuspecting people being unknowingly thrust into a world of horror and a cult that encourages or outright causes it all.  About the only thing that Callisto tried to do different, is the melee system, which has already been covered (its garbage).

With all this being said, and there is still much more that I could say about how bad the game is, let it suffice for me to just urge people to not buy this game.

It isn't worth it at full price

It isn't worth it at sale price

It isn't worth it if they decided to give it away for free.  

The TIME investment alone makes this game a bad choice, do yourself a favor, don't buy, get the Dead Space remake instead.

TLDR:
